area: sequencer run-time (executing sequences end to end)
verified_correct: Pause really stops capture: run 2 was paused at 3/4 exposures at 18:55:36; over the next 52s framesCaptured stayed 3, captured_images rows for producing_run_id=2 stayed 3, and the .fits count on disk stayed 7 (4 from run 1 + 3 from run 2). I attacked it by leaving it paused for ~17x the 3s exposure length, and by counting files on disk rather than trusting the counter.

A second run in the same app launch works: run 2 started at 18:54:28 in the same process that had already completed run 1 at 18:46:40, produced its own sequence_runs row (id=2) and captured frames normally. This was the previously-reported 'only one run per app launch' blocker; it is fixed in this build.

Frames claimed == rows in DB == files on disk for run 1: the Session Report said 'Frames accepted 4/4', stats_json framesCaptured=4, captured_images had exactly 4 rows, and the capture folder had exactly 4 .fits (plus 4 thumbnails). I checked the files by name and size (4150080 bytes each = 1920x1080x16bit + header), not just by count.
coverage_note: run 1 complete (status failed on Dither, 4/4 frames)

findings.title: Connecting the Built-in Multi-Star Guider is a silent no-op: no connection, no error, no UI change
findings.what_happened: Clicked Connect on 'Built-in Multi-Star Guider' (native) in Equipment > Discovery. The row stayed on 'Connect', the status bar stayed 'Guider Disconnected', the header count stayed '4 connected', and no snackbar/banner/error appeared. The log records only 'Connecting to Guider device: native:builtin_guider:multi_star' + 'Registered device from ID' and then nothing - no success line and no error line. Clicked Connect a second time 68s later: log again shows only 'Connecting to Guider device' with no follow-up. System Health silently dropped 100 -> 75 ('1 issue') after the first attempt.
findings.expected: Either the guider connects (row flips to Connected, status bar shows the guider), or the app tells the user why it failed. A connect that produces no state change and no message is indistinguishable from a dead button.
findings.repro: Fresh profile -> Equipment -> Discovery > Expand -> GUIDERS > Built-in Multi-Star Guider > Connect. Wait 15s. Re-read tree/status bar.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-11.png (row still shows Connect, footer 'Guider Disconnected'); /tmp/ns-audit/r-sequencer-run/app.log lines 103-105 and 18:31:41 entry
findings.where: Equipment > Discovery > Guiders row (native built-in guider)
findings.proposed_fix: Surface the failure: the native guider connect path must resolve to Ok/Err and the UI must show the Err. If the built-in guider requires a guide camera to be selected first, say so in the row instead of offering an inert Connect.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced on a fresh v-sequencer-run profile with camera+mount+focuser+filterwheel sims connected. Equipment > Discovery > GUIDERS > Built-in Multi-Star Guider > Connect does NOT fail silently: a modal 'Connection help' dialog appears headed 'The connection didn't complete', body 'The guide camera connection didn't complete and we couldn't pin down the exact cause', four numbered remediation steps, an expandable 'Technical details' with the raw driver message, and Close / 'Retry connection' actions (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vsr-10.png). Timing measured: first attempt surfaced the dialog ~13s after the click (log 'Connecting to Guider device' 16:03:40 -> dialog by 16:03:53, the native connect timeout); after closing it and clicking Connect again the dialog was back within 4s, twice in a row. The log evidence cited is accurate but the inference is wrong - the failure is reported through the UI, not the log. The row correctly stays 'Connect' and the status bar 'Guider Disconnected' because the connect really failed (built-in multi-star guider needs a guide camera; none assigned). System Health is not silent either: the STATUS card renders '75 - Good' with a '1 issue' chip and enumerates it. Most likely the original agent sampled the tree at t+15s, right at the first-attempt timeout, and never re-read.

findings.title: Pre-flight warns that a step is scheduled 'before target rises' when it is scheduled AFTER the rise time it prints
findings.what_happened: Pre-Flight Validation listed three warnings of the form: 'New Target: "Cool Camera" scheduled at 14:45 before target rises at 11:44' (also for Unpark Mount and Slew to Target at 14:55). 14:45 and 14:55 are both AFTER 11:44, and the target card for the same target shows Rise 11:44 / Transit 17:49 / Set 23:47, i.e. the target is up at run time. The warning states the opposite of the data on the adjacent card.
findings.expected: No warning at all for a step scheduled between rise and set. If the intent is 'before the NEXT rise', the message must name that time, not a rise that already happened.
findings.repro: Set site 30N/82E, build Target(RA 00h,Dec +00) with Cool Camera/Unpark/Slew/Autofocus/Take Exposures, press Start at 14:45 local. Read the Simulation section of the Pre-Flight dialog.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-39.png (three warning lines) and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-32.png (Rise 11:44, Transit 17:49, Set 23:47 for the same target)
findings.where: Sequencer > Builder > Start > Pre-Flight Validation > Simulation
findings.proposed_fix: Compare the scheduled instant against the rise/set interval that CONTAINS it; only warn when the step really falls outside the visibility window, and print the boundary that was violated.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced verbatim. Site 30N/82E, target 'New Target' RA 00h00m00s / Dec +00d00'36", Start pressed at 16:54 local. Pre-Flight > Simulation printed three warnings: 'New Target: "Cool Camera" scheduled at 16:54 before target rises at 11:36' plus the same for Dither (17:04) and Unpark Mount (17:05). All three times are AFTER the 11:36 it prints. I computed the true window independently from the app's own LST readout (LST 23:12 at 16:54 local): for RA 0h/Dec 0, rise is at LST 18h -> ~11:42 local and set at LST 6h -> ~23:42 local, so the target is genuinely above the horizon at run time and no conflict exists at all. Evidence /tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2/32.png.
findings.location_wrong: unit says screen:sequencer/preflight_validation_dialog.dart, but the dialog only renders the string. The comparison and the text live in SequenceTimeEstimator.findTimingConflicts, packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/sequence_time_estimator.dart:786-798 (the 'before target rises at' literal is line 791); _formatTime at line 411 prints HH:mm only, which is why a rise on a different calendar day reads as one that already passed.

findings.title: Pre-flight dark-library check uses the camera default temperature (-10C), not the temperature the sequence's Cool Camera node will actually reach (15C)
findings.what_happened: The sequence's Cool Camera node was set to Target Temperature 15C (confirmed on the node chip '15C' and in Properties). Pre-Flight's Dark Library section reported 'No matching darks found for 1 exposure combination: gain=100, offset=50, temp=-10.0C, duration=3s, binning=1x1'. During the run the camera reported Cam: 15.0C. The check therefore matched darks against a temperature the run never uses, and the 'Capture missing darks' action it offers would capture darks at the wrong temperature.
findings.expected: Dark matching should use the setpoint the sequence will actually be at (the Cool Camera node value, 15C), or say which temperature it assumed and why.
findings.repro: Add Cool Camera, set Target Temperature 15. Add Take Exposures 4x3s. Start -> read Pre-Flight > Dark Library.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-41.png ('temp=-10.0C'); /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-26.png (node set to 15C); /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-43.png (telemetry 'Cam: 15.0C' during the run)
findings.where: Sequencer > Builder > Start > Pre-Flight Validation > Dark Library
findings.proposed_fix: Resolve the planned sensor temperature from the sequence's cooling instruction chain before querying the dark library; fall back to the camera default only when no Cool Camera node precedes the exposures.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced. The sequence's Cool Camera node was set to Target Temperature 15 (node chip '15C', Properties field 15) and the run held 15.0C. Pre-Flight > Dark Library still reported 'No matching darks found for 1 exposure combination: gain=100, offset=50, temp=-10.0C, duration=3s, binning=1x1'. Evidence /tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2/32.png. Code confirms it is unconditional, not a race.
findings.location_wrong: unit says screen:sequencer/preflight_validation_dialog.dart; the temperature is chosen in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/rules/preflight_rules.dart:116-118 ('final cameraState = ref.read(cameraStateProvider); final camTargetTemp = cameraState.targetTemp;') and stamped onto every DarkFrameRequirement at line 139. Nothing there consults the sequence's CoolCameraNode.

findings.title: Pre-flight prints the same guider problem twice and both times tells you to connect PHD2, in a build that ships its own native guider
findings.what_happened: The General section lists 'No Guider Connected - This sequence includes guiding or dithering operations that require PHD2' immediately followed by 'Guider Not Connected - Dither requires a guider (PHD2) but none is connected.' Both carry the identical hint 'Connect to PHD2 in the Guiding panel.' Discovery in this same build offers a 'Built-in Multi-Star Guider (native)' with no PHD2 involved.
findings.expected: One warning per distinct problem, and advice that matches the guider backends this build actually offers.
findings.repro: Build any sequence containing a Dither node with no guider connected, press Start, scroll the Pre-Flight dialog.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-40.png
findings.where: Sequencer > Builder > Start > Pre-Flight Validation > General
findings.proposed_fix: De-duplicate the two rules and make the remediation text backend-aware ('Connect a guider in Equipment, or PHD2 in the Guiding panel').

findings.title: Node palette search ranks Smart Exposure above the node literally named 'Dither' when you search 'Dither'
findings.what_happened: Typing 'Dither' in the node palette search returns 'Smart Exposure' first (its description contains 'handles rotation + dither') and the node actually named 'Dither' second. Clicking the first result's + - the natural action after typing an exact node name - adds a Smart Exposure node instead. I hit this myself: the sequence silently gained an unwanted Smart Exposure node (visible only as the planned-frame count jumping from 4 to 8).
findings.expected: An exact name match ranks first. NINA's instruction search puts a literal name match at the top.
findings.repro: Sequencer > Builder > Nodes > search 'Dither'.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-30.png (Smart Exposure listed above Dither for the query 'Dither')
findings.where: Sequencer > Builder > Nodes palette
findings.proposed_fix: Score name matches above description matches; exact/prefix name match first.

findings.title: The '+' button on a palette node card does not add the node; only double-click does
findings.what_happened: Clicking the '+' affordance on the 'Dither' palette card only selected/highlighted the card - node count stayed at 10 and no Dither node appeared. Double-clicking the same card added it (count 10 -> 11). The '+' worked for other cards earlier in the session, so the affordance is inconsistent rather than absent.
findings.expected: The '+' on a palette card always appends that node.
findings.repro: Sequencer > Builder > search 'Dither' > click the '+' on the Dither card > check the node count in the sequence header. Then double-click the card.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-30.png and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-31.png (card highlighted, still '10 nodes'); node count went to 11 only after a double-click
findings.where: Sequencer > Builder > Nodes palette
findings.proposed_fix: Route the '+' tap through the same add-node handler as double-click and make sure the hit target is the icon, not the card body.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Does not reproduce on the rebuilt bundle. (a) Unfiltered palette: node count '1 node' -> ONE click on the '+' glyph of the Dither card -> '2 nodes / 1 step' with a Dither node in the sequence tree. (b) The finding's exact repro: typed 'Dither' into the palette search, single-clicked the '+' on the filtered Dither card -> '3 nodes / 2 steps'. No double-click used in either case. Code agrees and is not a post-finding fix: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/sequencer/widgets/node_palette.dart:800-812 wires the always-visible plus icon to GestureDetector(onTap: _addNode) with the comment 'Always-visible add button: a single tap adds the node ... Previously the only click-to-add affordance was a hidden double-tap', and git shows no uncommitted change to that file. Most likely the original observation missed the target: the plus is ~13px (Responsive.iconSize(context, 13), line 689) and a click a few pixels off lands on the card, which only selects it - exactly the reported symptom.

findings.title: Captured frames are written to the DB with NO gain, offset, sensor temperature, mount pointing, focuser position or target link - although the FITS file it just wrote has all of them
findings.what_happened: Run 1 captured 4 lights. The FITS header on disk is complete: GAIN=100, OFFSET=10, CCD-TEMP=15.0, SET-TEMP=15.0, RA=0.0/DEC=0.0, OBJCTRA/OBJCTDEC, FOCUSPOS=25074, FOCTEMP=20.0, SITELAT=30.0, SITELONG=82.0, OBJECT='New Target'. The matching captured_images rows have gain=NULL, offset=NULL, sensor_temp=NULL, cooler_power=NULL, mount_ra=NULL, mount_dec=NULL, mount_altitude=NULL, mount_azimuth=NULL, pier_side=NULL, focuser_position=NULL, focuser_temp=NULL, rotator_angle=NULL and target_id=NULL. Only hfr, star_count, eccentricity, filter, exposure_duration and binning were persisted.
findings.expected: Every value the capture pipeline already knows (it wrote them into the FITS header microseconds earlier) should land in captured_images. Everything downstream reads the DB, not the file: the dark library matches on gain/offset/temp/duration/binning, analytics plots temperature and HFR, project tracking counts frames per target.
findings.repro: Run any sequence with Cool Camera + Take Exposures against the simulators, then: sqlite3 <profile>/data/skotiq.db 'select gain,offset,sensor_temp,mount_ra,focuser_position,target_id from captured_images;' and compare with the FITS header of the same file.
findings.evidence: DB row 1: /tmp/ns-audit/r-sequencer-run/captures/New Target_nofilter_0001.fits -> gain,offset,sensor_temp,mount_ra,mount_dec,focuser_position,target_id all empty. FITS header of that same file: GAIN=100 OFFSET=10 CCD-TEMP=15.0 FOCUSPOS=25074 RA=0.0 DEC=0.0.
findings.where: Sequencer run -> captured_images persistence
findings.proposed_fix: Populate captured_images from the same metadata struct used to build the FITS header, in one place, so the two cannot diverge. Add a regression test asserting the DB row and the header agree field for field.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced from scratch. Sequence > New Target > Take Exposures 4x3s LIGHT (Filter empty, Gain/Offset left on profile defaults), run against the sims. FITS header of New Target_nofilter_0001.fits: GAIN=100, OFFSET=10, CCD-TEMP=20.0, XBINNING/YBINNING=1, SITELAT=30.0, SITELONG=82.0, RA=0.0, OBJCTRA='00 00 00.00', DEC=0.0, OBJCTDEC='+00 00 00.00', FOCUSPOS=25000, FOCTEMP=20.0, OBJECT='New Target'. The four matching captured_images rows: gain, offset, sensor_temp, cooler_power, mount_ra, mount_dec, mount_altitude, mount_azimuth, pier_side, focuser_position, focuser_temp, rotator_angle ALL NULL and target_id NULL, while hfr (2.48-2.53), star_count (39), eccentricity, filter, exposure_duration 3.0, bin_x and session_id were persisted - row-for-row as reported. Root cause splits in two, which matters for the fix: (a) sensor_temp, cooler_power, mount_*, pier_side, focuser_*, rotator_angle are not in insertSequenceFrame's INSERT column list at all, so that path can never write them; (b) gain/offset ARE passed but come from attribution.gain/offset (the ExposureNode's per-node override), not from what the camera actually used, so a node on profile defaults writes NULL while the FITS card says 100/10. target_id resolves from the sequence tree and stays NULL because an ad-hoc Target node has no `targets` row (that table is empty after the run) - the Session Report itself files the frames as 'Untargeted'. P1 stands: dark-library matching keys on gain/offset/temp/binning and analytics/project tracking read the DB, not the file.
findings.location_wrong: unit says 'screen:sequencer/sequencer_screen.dart'; the defect is packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/database/daos/images_dao.dart:657 (insertSequenceFrame) and its only production caller packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/sequence_executor/event_operations.dart:708. sequencer_screen.dart has nothing to do with capture persistence.

findings.title: Four surfaces disagree about which filter a frame was taken through: filename says 'nofilter', DB says 'R', FITS header has no FILTER card, run stats say 'Unknown'
findings.what_happened: For the same 4 frames of run 1: the files on disk are named 'New Target_nofilter_0001.fits'...'_0004.fits'; captured_images.filter = 'R' for all four; the FITS headers contain no FILTER keyword at all; the Session Report's Targets table shows Filter 'R'; and sequence_runs.stats_json targetBreakdown buckets them under filter key 'Unknown'. The live telemetry strip during the run showed 'Filter: R'.
findings.expected: One answer. If the wheel is on slot R, the filename, the FITS FILTER card, the DB column and the run stats all say R.
findings.repro: Connect the simulated filter wheel, run a Take Exposures node with no explicit filter, then compare ls of the capture folder, the FITS header, captured_images.filter, and stats_json.targetBreakdown.
findings.evidence: ls /tmp/ns-audit/r-sequencer-run/captures/ ; FITS header dump (no FILTER card); sqlite captured_images.filter='R'; sequence_runs.stats_json targetBreakdown {"New Sequence":{"Unknown":{...}}}; /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-44.png (Session Report shows Filter R)
findings.where: Sequencer run -> file naming / FITS writer / captured_images / run stats
findings.proposed_fix: Resolve the filter name once at exposure start and thread that single value into the filename template, the FITS FILTER card, the DB column and the stats bucket.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced with my own run (Target > Take Exposures 4x3s, node Filter empty - 'No filters in profile' - sim wheel parked on slot R). All five surfaces verified independently: (1) files on disk 'New Target_nofilter_0001..0004.fits'; (2) captured_images.filter = 'R' on all four rows; (3) the FITS header of _0001 has 27 cards and no FILTER card (dumped byte-wise, not via the app); (4) sequence_runs.stats_json = {"targetBreakdown":{"New Sequence":{"Unknown":{"captured":4,...}}}}; (5) the Session Report Targets table shows Filter 'R' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vsr-18.png). Two extras the finding missed: the same targetBreakdown keys the TARGET as 'New Sequence' (the sequence name) not 'New Target', and the Session Report labels the group 'Untargeted' - the breakdown is wrong on both axes. Severity corrected to P2: the frames really are taken through whatever slot the wheel sits on and the run is undamaged; the harm is downstream attribution ambiguity.
findings.location_wrong: unit says 'screen:sequencer/session_report_dialog.dart' - that dialog is one of five disagreeing readers and decides none of it. Writers: the Rust FITS/filename writer (no FILTER card, 'nofilter' token), event_operations.dart (~line 625: filter = progress.currentFilter ?? filterWheelStateProvider.currentFilterName), and whatever builds sequence_runs.stats_json targetBreakdown.

findings.title: Session report says 'Autofocus 0' after an autofocus that ran 9 points and completed successfully
findings.what_happened: Run 1 executed the Autofocus node: the live tree showed 'Autofocus - Point 5 of 9', the log shows 'Autofocus point 9 sample 1/1 completed' and "Child 'Autofocus' completed with status: Success", and the focuser moved from 25000 to 25074. The Session Report's Mount/Focus block shows Autofocus '0', and sequence_runs.stats_json has "autofocusRuns":0. focus_models is also empty (0 rows).
findings.expected: autofocusRuns == 1, and the report should show the resulting focus position / HFR so the user can tell whether focus was achieved.
findings.repro: Add an Autofocus node to a sequence, run it, open the Session Report and read the Autofocus counter; compare with app.log 'completed with status: Success'.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-44.png (Autofocus 0); /tmp/ns-audit/r-sequencer-run/app.log 18:47:36 "Child 'Autofocus' completed with status: Success"; stats_json autofocusRuns:0; focuser 25000 -> 25074
findings.where: Sequencer > Session Report > Mount & focus block; sequence_runs.stats_json
findings.proposed_fix: Increment the autofocus counter where the AutofocusNode reports Success, not where the (unused) focus-model persistence path runs.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced. Run 2 executed the Autofocus node: app.log shows 'Autofocus point 1..9 sample 1/1 completed' and "Child 'Autofocus' completed with status: Success" at 21:01:46Z, and the focuser moved 25000 -> 25070. The Session Report's Mount / operations block reads 'Autofocus runs 0' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2/39.png), sequence_runs id=2 stats_json has autofocusRuns:0, imaging_sessions.autofocus_count is 0, and focus_models has 0 rows. Root cause is total and mechanical: SequenceRunStats.recordAutofocus() (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence_stats_provider.dart:160) has ZERO non-test call sites - grep for 'recordAutofocus()' returns only the definition - so the counter can never be anything but 0. recordTriggerFire and recordMeridianFlip, by contrast, are wired up at event_operations.dart:317 and :926.

findings.title: Frames captured under a named target are reported as 'Untargeted', and the run's target breakdown is keyed by the SEQUENCE name instead of the target name
findings.what_happened: The sequence had exactly one Target node called 'New Target' and every exposure ran underneath it (the FITS OBJECT card and the filenames both say 'New Target'). The Session Report's Targets section shows a single group titled 'Untargeted - 4/4 frames | 12s'. sequence_runs.stats_json targetBreakdown is {"New Sequence": {"Unknown": {...}}} - keyed by the sequence's name, not the target's. captured_images.target_id is NULL for all 4 rows.
findings.expected: 'New Target - 4/4 frames', targetBreakdown keyed 'New Target', and captured_images.target_id pointing at that target.
findings.repro: Build Target 'New Target' with Take Exposures under it, run, open the Session Report and read the Targets section; then read stats_json.targetBreakdown.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-44.png ('Untargeted 4/4 frames'); stats_json targetBreakdown {"New Sequence":{"Unknown":...}}; captured_images.target_id NULL x4
findings.where: Sequencer > Session Report > Targets; sequence_runs.stats_json
findings.proposed_fix: Attribute each frame to the enclosing TargetHeaderNode (the executor already knows it - the filename template resolves the target name) and persist the target id on the captured_images row.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced exactly. Sequence 'New Sequence' with one Target node named 'New Target'; all 4 lights ran under it. Session Report > Targets shows a single group 'Untargeted  4/4 frames | 1m 20s' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2/39.png). sequence_runs id=2 stats_json targetBreakdown is {"New Sequence": {"Unknown": {captured:4,...}}} - keyed by the SEQUENCE name, filter 'Unknown' even though captured_images.filter is 'R'. captured_images.target_id is empty for all 4 rows and the targets table has 0 rows. The keying is the documented fallback chain at packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/sequence_executor/event_operations.dart:877-883: target = progress.currentTarget ?? currentSequenceProvider.name ?? 'Sequence', i.e. currentTarget was never populated (no TargetStarted/TargetChanged consumed) so it fell through to the sequence name.

findings.title: A single failing Dither node is reported as two identical errors, in the report and in two stacked critical banners
findings.what_happened: The sequence contains one Dither node. With no guider connected it failed once, but the run recorded errorMessages: ['Dither: Dither failed: No active guider configured', 'Dither: Dither failed: No active guider configured'], the Session Report's Errors section printed the line twice, and two identical 'Critical - Sequencer / Dither: Dither failed: No active guider configured' banners stacked on the right edge of the screen.
findings.expected: One error per failure occurrence.
findings.repro: Add one Dither node with no guider connected, run the sequence, read the Session Report Errors list and the on-screen banners.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-44.png (two identical Errors lines and two identical critical banners); sequence_runs.stats_json errorMessages array of length 2 for one node
findings.where: Sequencer run-time error reporting
findings.proposed_fix: Emit the failure once from the node executor; the second copy looks like the node-level and run-level handlers both recording it.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced. Exactly ONE Dither node, no guider connected. The native log records the failure exactly once ('ERROR Dither failed: Dither failed: No active guider configured' at 20:58:06Z, then a single "Child 'Dither' completed with status: Failure"), and the in-tree node error line renders once. But sequence_runs id=1 stats_json errorMessages has the identical string TWICE, and the Session Report's Errors section prints it twice (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2/35.png). One failure -> two recorded errors. Caveat: I did not catch the two stacked critical banners (already cleared when I looked), so that half is unverified; the report/DB half stands on its own.
findings.location_wrong: unit says screen:sequencer/run_dashboard/critical_event_banner.dart, but the duplication is upstream - the run's error list already holds two copies, so the banner just renders what it is given. SequenceRunStats.recordError (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence_stats_provider.dart:162) has no de-dup, unlike recordWarning at :166 which does. Point a fixer at the executor's error-recording path.

findings.title: The top-bar run chip still reads 'Sequence Running' (green) while the sequence is paused
findings.what_happened: With run 2 paused at 3/4 exposures (toolbar chip 'Paused 75%', node badge 'PAUSED', Pause button flipped to Resume, and no further frames being captured), the chip in the Sequencer's top tab bar - the app's most prominent run indicator - still showed a green dot and the text 'Sequence Running'. The accessibility tree confirms both strings are present simultaneously: 'panel: Sequence Running' and 'panel: Paused 75%'.
findings.expected: The top-bar chip should read Paused (amber) when the run is paused. Two indicators one row apart must not disagree about whether the rig is exposing.
findings.repro: Start a sequence, wait for exposures, click Pause, read the chip next to the Builder/Templates/Sequences/History tabs and compare with the toolbar chip.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-50.png (green 'Sequence Running' chip while paused); tree output showing 'Sequence Running', 'Paused 75%', 'PAUSED' at the same instant
findings.where: Sequencer > top tab bar run chip
findings.proposed_fix: Drive the chip from the same run-state enum as the toolbar chip instead of a boolean isRunning.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced. Run 3 paused at 17:06:37 mid-exposure. At 17:06:41 the accessibility tree simultaneously carried 'PAUSED' (node badge), 'panel: Sequence Running', 'Paused 25%' (toolbar chip) and a 'Resume' button; 45 seconds later progress was still frozen at 2/4 with 'Paused 50%'. The cropped capture of the Sequencer tab row (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2/40.png) shows the chip rendered with a GREEN dot and the literal text 'Sequence Running' at that moment. The finding's location is correct: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/sequencer/sequencer_screen_parts/tab_bar.dart:112 hard-codes 'Sequence Running' with colors.success and there is no paused variant.

findings.title: sequence_runs.status stays 'running' while the run is paused, so any non-GUI consumer thinks the rig is still exposing
findings.what_happened: During a 52-second pause of run 2 the DB row kept status='running'. The GUI knew it was paused, but the persisted state (which the headless API, the web dashboard and the mobile client read) did not distinguish paused from running.
findings.expected: A 'paused' status (or a paused_at column) so remote surfaces can show the true state.
findings.repro: Pause a run, then: sqlite3 <profile>/data/skotiq.db "select status from sequence_runs where id=2;"
findings.evidence: status='running' at 18:55:36 (paused) and still 'running' at 18:56:28, while the GUI showed PAUSED throughout
findings.where: sequence_runs table / run state persistence
findings.proposed_fix: Persist the paused state on pause and clear it on resume.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced and additionally proven from the schema. Run 3 paused at 17:06:37; sqlite3 on /tmp/ns-audit/v2-sequencer-run/data/skotiq.db returned status='running' for id=3 at 17:06:41 and still 'running' at 17:06:59, while the GUI showed PAUSED / 'Paused 50%' / Resume and frame progress was frozen. The table cannot express the state: .schema sequence_runs is (id, sequence_id, sequence_name, started_at, ended_at, status TEXT DEFAULT 'running', stats_json, sequence_snapshot_json) - no paused_at column, and 'paused' is never written mid-run (a terminal 'paused-stopped' is written only after Stop).
findings.severity_note: P2 (raised from P3) - this is the same single defect as the P2 top-bar-chip finding (no paused state is modelled anywhere), and this is the half that reaches unattended remote operators who have no GUI to correct them.

findings.title: The Continue Session handoff dialog says 'Unknown Profile' and 'No Sequence' while naming the sequence in its own header and with a real profile active
findings.what_happened: Relaunching the app after a night's session shows the Continue Session dialog titled 'New Sequence', with the rows 'Equipment Profile: Unknown Profile' and 'Sequence: No Sequence', above a primary button 'Load Previous Setup'. The scratch DB has exactly one equipment profile named 'My Equipment' (which the status bar shows as active) and one sequence named 'New Sequence' (which the dialog's own header prints, and which the dashboard card behind it names too). Both fields the dialog needs to restore are unresolved nulls: quick_start_dialog.dart:184-185 falls back to 'Unknown Profile'/'No Sequence' when quickStartContext.profileName/sequenceName are null.
findings.expected: 'Equipment Profile: My Equipment', 'Sequence: New Sequence'. This is the dialog whose whole purpose is telling you what it is about to restore; if it cannot name it, the user cannot trust the button.
findings.repro: Run a sequence, quit the app, relaunch on the same profile. Read the Continue Session dialog.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-60.png; sqlite3 skotiq.db 'select id,name from equipment_profiles' -> 1|My Equipment; sequence_runs row 2 named 'New Sequence'
findings.where: App launch > Continue Session (quick start / session handoff) dialog
findings.proposed_fix: Populate quickStartContext.profileName/sequenceName from the persisted last-run row (sequence_runs.sequence_name and the active profile) instead of from in-memory state that is empty on a cold start.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced on relaunch. Dialog titled 'Continue Session', card header prints 'New Sequence', and directly beneath it 'Equipment Profile: Unknown Profile' and 'Sequence: No Sequence' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2/42.png). The DB has exactly one equipment profile, 'My Equipment', which the status bar shows as active. The cited file:line is correct - quick_start_dialog.dart:184-185 reads 'profileName ?? \'Unknown Profile\'' and 'sequenceName ?? \'No Sequence\''. I also found the upstream cause the finding did not: the run's own imaging_sessions rows are written with profile_id NULL and sequence_id NULL (select id,profile_id,sequence_id from imaging_sessions -> 1||, 2||, 3||), and QuickStartService builds the context from imaging_sessions (quick_start_service.dart:624). Changing the fallback string alone would not fix it.
findings.location_wrong: unit says screen:sequencer/session_handoff_dialog.dart. The dialog that shows this is packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/quick_start_dialog.dart (the finding's own body names it correctly); session_handoff_dialog.dart exists but is a different surface.

findings.title: Quick-Start Wizard opens as an empty black panel with no content, no controls and no accessibility nodes
findings.what_happened: Sequencer > Builder > toolbar wand icon ('Quick-Start Wizard') opens a full-height ~960x555 solid black panel over the builder. After 90 seconds it still contained nothing: no title, no step rail, no Next/Cancel, no close affordance. The accessibility tree during that whole time contained zero wizard nodes - it still enumerated the underlying Builder tree - so this is not merely a paint problem, the dialog's semantics were never built.
findings.expected: The wizard's first step (target selection) with Next/Cancel, per _wizard_shell.dart.
findings.repro: Sequencer > Builder (sequence 'New Sequence', 4 sim devices connected) > click the wand icon in the toolbar. Wait.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-66.png (t+4s), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-67.png (t+30s), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-68.png (t+90s) - identical blank black panel; 'tree' over the same span shows no wizard nodes
findings.where: Sequencer > Builder > toolbar > Quick-Start Wizard
findings.proposed_fix: The wizard is the advertised fast path to a first sequence; a blank modal here is the worst possible first-run experience. Find the build-time exception (nothing appears in the native log, so it is Flutter-side) and add a fallback error state so a failed wizard says why instead of showing a black rectangle.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Same entry point (Sequencer > Builder > toolbar wand icon, 4 sim devices connected, empty 'New Sequence') and the wizard renders completely. Within ~5s the accessibility tree held 'Quick-Start Sequence Wizard / Step 1 of 5: Choose Your Target', the body 'Search for a target or enter coordinates manually.', three text fields (Target Name, Right Ascension, Declination) and both actions (Cancel, Next) - the direct opposite of the finding's load-bearing claim that the tree contained zero wizard nodes. /tmp/ns-audit/shots/vsr-12.png shows it fully painted: title, subtitle, 5-segment step rail with segment 1 filled, search field, RA/Dec pair, Cancel/Next footer. Cancelled and reopened; identical the second time. If the original agent saw a black rectangle it was a one-off softpipe paint fault, not a wizard defect - and the 'semantics were never built' claim would send a fixer into _wizard_shell.dart after a bug that is not there.

findings.title: Continue Session dialog dates yesterday's session as 'Today at 14:57'
findings.what_happened: Relaunched the app on 2026-08-02 at 10:40 local. The Continue Session dialog header reads 'Today at 14:57'. The session it refers to is sequence_runs id=2, ended_at=1785610650 = Sat Aug 1 14:57:30 EDT - i.e. YESTERDAY. The dashboard card behind the same dialog gets it right ('Completed - 19 hours ago') and the app's own date header says 'Sun Aug 2'. So two surfaces one dialog apart disagree about which day the run happened, and the modal one is wrong.
findings.expected: 'Yesterday at 14:57' (or the date). A handoff dialog exists to tell you whether the state it is about to restore is from the night you are still in; getting the day wrong defeats its only job.
findings.repro: Run a sequence, quit, relaunch the app the next calendar day, read the Continue Session dialog header.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-71.png ('Continue Session / Today at 14:57' over a card reading 'Completed - 19 hours ago'); sqlite3 skotiq.db 'select ended_at from sequence_runs where id=2' -> 1785610650 -> Sat Aug 1 14:57:30 EDT 2026; system date Sun Aug 2 10:40
findings.where: App launch > Continue Session dialog header
findings.proposed_fix: Format the timestamp with a calendar-day comparison (today / yesterday / explicit date) instead of assuming the last session is from the current day.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced deliberately. I backdated the audit profile's imaging_sessions rows by 19 hours (last session end_time -> 2026-08-02 22:03:07 local, i.e. YESTERDAY) and relaunched at 2026-08-03 17:10. The dialog header printed 'Continue Session / Today at 22:03' while the dashboard card one layer behind it correctly read 'Paused-stopped - 19 hours ago' and the briefing header said 'Mon Aug 3' - all three visible in /tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2/42.png. The bug is unconditional in quick_start_dialog.dart:103-116: _formatDate compares ELAPSED time ('final diff = now.difference(dt); if (diff.inDays == 0) return \'Today at ...\''), so any session under 24h old is labelled Today regardless of calendar day, and 'Yesterday' can only ever appear for sessions 24-48h old.
findings.location_wrong: unit says screen:sequencer/session_handoff_dialog.dart; the code is packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/quick_start_dialog.dart:103-116. The finding's repro also attributes the timestamp to sequence_runs.ended_at - it is not: I shifted sequence_runs by 19h and the header did not move at all. The date comes from imaging_sessions.end_time via QuickStartService (quick_start_service.dart:624).

findings.title: Continue Session reports '0 minutes integration' for a session that has 12s of integration on the card behind it
findings.what_happened: The dialog's Progress row reads '4/4 frames captured, 0 minutes integration'. The dashboard card for the same run reads '12s integration'. Integration time is rounded to whole minutes, so any sub-minute (and any 90s) session is reported as 0 or as a truncated value.
findings.expected: Match the rest of the app: '12s integration'. Reporting real captured photons as '0 minutes' is the sort of thing that makes a user think the run did nothing.
findings.repro: Run a short sequence (4 x 3s), relaunch, read the Continue Session Progress row and compare with the dashboard's last-run card.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-71.png - '4/4 frames captured, 0 minutes integration' next to a card reading '12s integration | 4 frames | 3m 2s duration'
findings.where: App launch > Continue Session > Progress row
findings.proposed_fix: Use the same duration formatter as the dashboard card (h/m/s), not integer minutes.

findings.title: 'Load Previous Setup' is inert: it restores no equipment, no sequence and writes nothing to the log - it just closes the dialog
findings.what_happened: On relaunch I clicked the Continue Session dialog's primary button 'Load Previous Setup' (the only styled action; 'Skip' is the secondary). The dialog closed and NOTHING else changed: the status bar still read Camera Disconnected / Mount Disconnected / Guider Disconnected / Focus ---, the profile chip still read 'My Equipment 0/0', the Sequencer builder still held an empty 'New Sequence' with '0 targets / Sequence 0 steps', and app.log recorded not one line between the click at 10:41:30 and 10:42:40 (no connect attempt, no sequence load, no error). The previous session had 4 connected simulators and a 5-node sequence.
findings.expected: Either it reconnects the previous equipment and loads the previous sequence, or - if it cannot resolve them, which it already admits by printing 'Unknown Profile' and 'No Sequence' - the button is disabled with an explanation. A primary action that silently no-ops is worse than no button: after a crash mid-night this is the control a user reaches for first.
findings.repro: Run a sequence with simulators connected, quit the app, relaunch, click 'Load Previous Setup', then read the status bar, the profile chip and the Sequencer builder.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-71.png (dialog); tree after the click shows 'Camera Disconnected', 'Mount Disconnected', 'My Equipment 0/0', 'New Sequence / 0 targets / Sequence 0 steps'; /tmp/ns-audit/r-sequencer-run/app.log has zero entries in the 70s following the click
findings.where: App launch > Continue Session > Load Previous Setup
findings.proposed_fix: Wire the button to the same restore path the profile auto-connect uses, and gate it on the context actually resolving (same nulls that produce 'Unknown Profile'/'No Sequence' should disable it).
findings.verdict_reasoning: The no-op is real; the 'silent' half is not, and the truth is worse. Four completed runs with 4 sims connected, quit, relaunch: the 'Continue Session' dialog appears with 'Equipment Profile: Unknown Profile / Sequence: No Sequence / Progress 4/4 frames captured' and 'Load Previous Setup' as primary (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vseqrun-42.png). Clicking it restores nothing - status bar still Camera/Mount/Guider Disconnected, Focus '---', profile chip 'My Equipment 0/0'. But it is NOT silent: a full-width green success snackbar reads 'Loaded previous setup for previous target from frame 1' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vseqrun-43.png and the same string in the a11y tree). So this is a false-success claim, not a dead button - cry-wolf class, and it changes the fix. The finding's log evidence proves nothing: app.log is the Rust tracing stream only and contains no Dart-side lines at all (zero 'QuickStart'/'SequenceExecutor'/'ImagesDao' sources in 904 lines of mine or in the original agent's), so the Dart logger's 'Starting fresh with context:' line could never appear there. Mechanism: _handleStartFresh only acts when context.profileId / context.sequenceId are non-null plus the equipment snapshot; all four of my imaging_sessions rows have profile_id NULL, sequence_id NULL and empty equipment_snapshot, so there is genuinely nothing to restore - the dialog already says so and then offers the action anyway and reports success. Fixes: disable/relabel the primary when the snapshot is empty, and/or stamp profile_id/sequence_id/equipment_snapshot onto imaging_sessions. P2: no data lost, the damage is the false claim.
findings.location_wrong: unit says 'screen:sequencer/session_handoff_dialog.dart'. The dialog is packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/quick_start_dialog.dart ('Load Previous Setup' label at line 407) and the behaviour is packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/quick_start_checker.dart:_handleStartFresh (~line 244). session_handoff_service.dart is a different feature (cross-device carry-over).

findings.title: Builder and Pre-Flight disagree about how long the same sequence takes: '~18m 54s' vs 'Duration 27m'
findings.what_happened: The identical 7-step sequence (Cool 15C, Slew, Autofocus, 4x3s lights, Unpark, Park, Warm 20C @2C/min) is estimated at '~18m 54s' by the estimate chip in the Builder header and at 'Duration 27m / Ends 11:20' by the Pre-Flight Simulation panel, both visible in the same screenshot with the dialog open over the builder. That is a 43% disagreement. The header estimate also did not move at all when I changed the Cool Camera setpoint from -10C to +15C (ambient 20C), i.e. after removing ~25C of cooling work the builder still printed exactly ~18m 54s.
findings.expected: One estimate, computed once. Session planning (will this finish before dawn?) depends on it, and the pre-flight's 'Ends 11:20' is what a user schedules around.
findings.repro: Builder: add Cool Camera / Slew / Autofocus / Take Exposures 4x3s / Unpark / Park / Warm Camera. Read the estimate chip next to the sequence header. Press Start and read Simulation > Duration.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-84.png - builder chip '~18m 54s' at the top right of the tree, dialog panel 'Duration 27m', 'Ends 11:20', taken 10:53:40
findings.where: Sequencer > Builder header estimate vs Start > Pre-Flight > Simulation
findings.proposed_fix: Have both surfaces call the same estimator; if the pre-flight adds slew/settle/overheads the builder does not, show the same breakdown in both instead of two bare numbers.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced with my own sequence (Target > Cool Camera 15C, Dither, Unpark, Slew, Autofocus, Take Exposures 4x3s). In one frame (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2/32.png): Builder header estimate chip '~14m 9s'; Pre-Flight > Simulation 'Duration 12m' and 'Ends 17:07' against a 16:54 start (= 13m implied). Three different numbers for the same sequence. Note also the Cool Camera Properties panel shows 'Max cooling time 10m / Duration: 10m / Contributes 29.3% of total', i.e. the Builder bills the node's Max Duration, which makes the finding's secondary claim (estimate does not move when the setpoint changes) plausible - I did not isolate that sub-claim.
findings.location_wrong: unit says screen:sequencer/preflight_validation_dialog.dart, which is only one of the two disagreeing sides. The Builder chip/timeline uses SequenceTimeEstimator (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/sequence_time_estimator.dart, called from screens/sequencer/widgets/node_timing_section.dart:119-128 and sequence_timeline.dart:55-65); the Pre-Flight panel uses PreSessionSimulator().simulate(...) (preflight_validation_dialog.dart:134, rendered at :735). Two engines, not one dialog.
findings.severity_note: P2 (unchanged) - but the magnitude I measured is ~18%, not the 43% claimed; the disagreement itself is real and simultaneous on one screen.

findings.title: A node can only be reordered by drag; the node context menu offers just Duplicate and Delete
findings.what_happened: After adding Unpark Mount late (it appended to the end, after Take Exposures) the only way to move it earlier is drag-and-drop: right-clicking the node yields a popup menu containing exactly two items, 'Duplicate' and 'Delete' (accessibility tree: 'panel: Popup menu / button: Duplicate / button: Delete'). There is no Move Up / Move Down / Cut / Paste, and no keyboard equivalent. My drag attempt (press, 9 intermediate moves, release over the target row) left the order unchanged.
findings.expected: Move up / move down (or cut+paste) in the context menu, as NINA and SGP both provide. Order is semantically load-bearing here - unpark must precede slew - and a sequence with 30 instructions is not comfortably reordered by dragging in a scrolling tree.
findings.repro: Sequencer > Builder > add any node > right-click it > read the menu.
findings.evidence: tree after right-click on 'Unpark Mount': 'panel: Popup menu', 'button: Duplicate', 'button: Delete' and nothing else; /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-80.png shows the resulting wrong order (Take Exposures above Unpark Mount)
findings.where: Sequencer > Builder > node context menu
findings.proposed_fix: Add Move Up / Move Down / Indent / Outdent to the context menu and bind them to Alt+Arrow.

findings.title: The Builder tree shows a different instruction ORDER than the one that executes (drag-reorder mutates the model but never repaints)
findings.what_happened: I dragged 'Unpark Mount' from the bottom of the list up onto the 'Slew to Target' row. The tree did not change: before and after the drag it read Cool Camera, Slew to Target, Autofocus, Take Exposures, Unpark Mount, Park Mount, Warm Camera - so I concluded the drag had failed. It had not. When I ran the sequence the executor enumerated 'Child 0: Cool Camera, Child 1: Unpark Mount, Child 2: Slew to Target, Child 3: Autofocus, Child 4: Take Exposures, Child 5: Park Mount, Child 6: Warm Camera' and ran it in that order. The stale view survived the run, the Session Report and a second run: at 10:57 the accessibility tree still listed Unpark fifth while run 4's executor listed it second.
findings.expected: The tree is the sequence. Either the drop is rejected and nothing moves, or the drop is applied and the tree repaints. A builder that silently executes an order different from the one it is displaying is the single most dangerous thing a sequencer can do - the displayed order here happens to be the unsafe one (slew with a parked mount), and a user reading the screen has no way to know what will actually run.
findings.repro: Sequencer > Builder > add Cool Camera, Slew to Target, Autofocus, Take Exposures, then Unpark Mount (it appends last) > drag Unpark up onto the Slew row > read the tree (unchanged) > press Start > read app.log's 'Child N:' enumeration.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-80.png (tree: ... Take Exposures, Unpark Mount, Park Mount, Warm Camera); accessibility tree at 10:56 lists the same order; /tmp/ns-audit/r-sequencer-run/app.log 14:54:37 and 14:57:12 both enumerate 'Child 1: Unpark Mount' / 'Child 2: Slew to Target'
findings.where: Sequencer > Builder > sequence tree (drag reorder)
findings.proposed_fix: The reorder mutates the node list without invalidating the tree's provider/state. Make the drop go through the same state notifier the add path uses so the widget rebuilds, and add a test that asserts the rendered order equals the model order after a reorder.
findings.verdict_reasoning: I reproduced the divergence and then found it is between the EXECUTOR and the ACCESSIBILITY TREE, not between the executor and the screen - the symptom is a harness artifact and the stated cause is wrong. Method: Sequence = [Slew to Target (custom RA 17h/Dec+30), Unpark Mount, Take Exposures 4x3s], dragged rows with synthetic press-move-release. Drops on a card body are rejected; drops on the dashed 'Insert here' zone are accepted. After an accepted drop of Take Exposures to the head, `tree` still enumerated Slew / Unpark / Take Exposures and run 3's executor logged 'Child 0: Take Exposures, Child 1: Slew to Target, Child 2: Unpark Mount' and ran it that way - exactly the finding's evidence. But screenshots taken at the same time (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vseqrun-37.png, -38.png) show the visible builder already in the new order. I then made it unambiguous: dragged Take Exposures down one slot and screenshotted 1.5s after mouseup (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vseqrun-41.png) - the painted list reads Slew, Take Exposures, Unpark (repainted immediately) while `tree` at that same moment still read Slew, Unpark, Take Exposures; run 4's executor then logged 'Child 0: Slew to Target, Child 1: Take Exposures, Child 2: Unpark Mount'. So executor == painted order != AT-SPI order. The AT-SPI child enumeration keeps pre-drag creation order and never re-sorts: a real but P3 accessibility defect (a screen-reader user hears the wrong order), not 'the screen lies about what will run'. Also flag: the finding's only screenshot evidence, /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-80.png, has 10:50:45 on the app clock while its own drag+run citations are 10:54-10:57 - that image is the PRE-drag state and never showed a stale post-drag view.
findings.location_wrong: unit says 'screen:sequencer/sequencer_screen.dart' for a repaint bug that does not exist; the real, much smaller defect is the semantics/a11y ordering of the instruction list, not its painting.

findings.title: Light frames are written with NO pointing at all - no RA/DEC/OBJCTRA/OBJECT card and NULL mount_ra/mount_dec - after a successful slew to explicit coordinates
findings.what_happened: Run 4 slewed the mount to RA 17.0000h Dec +30.0000 ('Slewing mount sim_mount_1 to RA=17.0000h Dec=30.0000', Slew completed Success at 14:57:13) and then captured 4 lights at 14:58:02-14:58:14. The FITS headers of those frames contain SIMPLE/BITPIX/NAXIS/EXPTIME/DATE-OBS/IMAGETYP/GAIN/OFFSET/CCD-TEMP/SET-TEMP/XBINNING/YBINNING/SITELAT/SITELONG/FOCUSPOS/FOCTEMP/NS-SESID/NS-FIDX/NS-NPLN - and nothing else. There is no RA, DEC, OBJCTRA, OBJCTDEC, OBJECT or FILTER card. captured_images.mount_ra / mount_dec / target_id are NULL for the same four rows. So after the run there is no record anywhere of where the telescope was pointed. (Frames taken under a Target node in run 1 did get RA/DEC cards, so the writer only emits pointing when a Target group exists, not when the mount is simply on target.)
findings.expected: Every light frame carries the mount's actual RA/DEC at exposure start, regardless of whether the coordinates came from a Target group or from a Slew node's custom coordinates. This is basic FITS hygiene: stacking software, plate-solve verification and the app's own project tracking all key off it, and a sequence built around Slew-with-custom-coordinates (the flow the app itself pushes you to when it warns 'No target group found in sequence') silently produces unlabelled data.
findings.repro: Builder: Cool Camera, Unpark, Slew to Target with Use Target Coordinates OFF and RA 17.0 / Dec 30.0, Autofocus, Take Exposures 4x3s, Park, Warm. Run to completion. Then dump the FITS header of any captured frame and select mount_ra,mount_dec from captured_images.
findings.evidence: Header dump of /tmp/ns-audit/r-sequencer-run/captures/untargeted_nofilter_0001.fits (23 cards, no RA/DEC/OBJECT); sqlite 'select mount_ra,mount_dec,target_id from captured_images where producing_run_id=4' -> all NULL; app.log 14:57:12 'Slewing to RA: 17.0000h, Dec: 30.0000'
findings.where: Sequencer run -> FITS writer / captured_images
findings.proposed_fix: Read the mount's current RA/DEC from the device at exposure start and always write RA/DEC (plus OBJCTRA/OBJCTDEC) and persist them; fall back to the target group only for the OBJECT name.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced end to end. Sequence with NO Target group: Slew to Target with 'Use Target Coordinates' OFF and RA 17.0000h / Dec 30.0000, then Take Exposures 4x3s LIGHT. Log: 'Slewing to RA: 17.0000h, Dec: 30.0000', 'Slewing mount sim_mount_1 to RA=17.0000h Dec=30.0000', then Child 'Slew to Target' completed with status: Success before the exposures. The four files (untargeted_nofilter_0001..0004.fits) have exactly 22 cards: SIMPLE, BITPIX, NAXIS, NAXIS1/2, BZERO, BSCALE, EXPTIME, DATE-OBS, IMAGETYP, GAIN, OFFSET, CCD-TEMP, XBINNING, YBINNING, SITELAT, SITELONG, FOCUSPOS, FOCTEMP, NS-SESID, NS-FIDX, NS-NPLN - no RA, DEC, OBJCTRA, OBJCTDEC, OBJECT or FILTER. captured_images rows 5-8 (producing_run_id=2): mount_ra, mount_dec, target_id all NULL. Control: the earlier Target-group run in the same app instance DID emit RA/OBJCTRA/DEC/OBJCTDEC/OBJECT, confirming pointing is emitted only when a Target group exists. One correction that matters for the fix: even in the working case the RA/DEC written are the TARGET's coordinates (0.0/0.0 for an unedited 'New Target'), not the mount's reported position - the writer never reads mount pointing at all, so 'every light frame carries the mount's actual RA/DEC' is not satisfied by either path. P1 stands: a night shot via Slew-with-custom-coordinates leaves no pointing record on disk or in the DB.
findings.location_wrong: unit 'seq-node:ExposureNode' is approximately right for the FITS half (the header is assembled on the Rust capture path from the sequence context); the DB half belongs to images_dao.dart insertSequenceFrame + event_operations.dart, not the node.
